answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying trading limits to a verified history of useful work. Each agent must complete auditable tasks that independent peers attest, building reputation slowly like quartz forming under pressure. A newcomer can sign a small deal with a quill, but large deals require a long record. Spinning up a thousand fakes creates no shortcut: each identity must repeat the same costly work, so the ripple of one bad actor stays small while the cost of a mass forgery grows with every copy.
